title: Reconcile token scopes and rebuild auto-layout flows for dense table components
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Several dense table variants (row-dense / compact / stacked) were forked historically to support local product needs. Over time token scope drifted: some variants reference global semantic tokens, others rely on local overrides and hard-coded spacing. Auto-layout anchors are inconsistent across instances which causes visual jitter when nested inside cards or responsive containers. This ticket aims to: 1) audit and reconcile token scopes for table primitives (row, cell, header, divider); 2) migrate legacy local overrides into a small set of controlled variant flags; 3) rebuild the auto-layout constraint flow so that tables behave predictably when resized or when density tokens change; and 4) add publish gating + lint checks to prevent future regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All table primitives use either a documented global semantic token or a named local token group (no hard-coded px on primary components)
Three canonical density variants (comfortable, compact, dense) exist as first-class variants on the master table component with toggles for rowHeight and cellPadding
Auto-layout constraints for header, body and row items are rebuilt so that expanding cell content does not collapse neighboring columns; verified on breakpoints 320/768/1280
Figma library publish runs without errors and includes a migration note; at least two downstream pages (dashboard and reports) validated with no layout regressions
A small Node-based CLI lint rule (run during publish) flags local overrides of spacing tokens and returns non-zero exit code if present
